newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hits day's low under $18 on OPEC, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hits day's low under $18 on OPEC, NYMEX.

text.p: IPE August Brent on Thursday fell below psychological support at $18 a barrel on Thursday to a session low of $17.89 in choppy trade after NYMEX's lower opening, brokers said.

August IPE Brent futures were trading 32 cents lower at $17.90 a barrel at 1434 GMT in see-saw action after a morning of losses inspired by scepticism over OPEC's ability to stick to renewed pledges of quota adherence.
"It's bearish with support at $17.90/95," a Brent crude broker said.
"It looks very mixed at the moment, but I certainly wouldn't attach any bullish weight to whatever is coming out of OPEC," said another.
Brokers said bears had taken heart from an OPEC denial that Venezuela had admitted overproducing at the group's six-monthly talks in Vienna this week.

Brokers said any such admission would have been a constructive sign that members were facing reality and prepared to work to achieve a solution. The denial implied face-saving for quota-busters was more important than price support, they said.
IPE July gas oil was trading $1.50 firmer at $161.75 a tonne, catching up on Brent's late gains yesterday.
Brent made a big 34-cent gain on Wednesday following declarations by OPEC that it would cut back on over-production.

OPEC leaders on Thursday confirmed the previous day's deal to stick to previously agreed production ceilings. Market doubt swung on statements by Venezuelan oil minister Erwin Arrieta that his country was not over-producing.
His remarks raised eyebrows as his country is assessed to be pumping out 800,000 bpd over its quota.
